text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet will propose changes in local foreign exchange trade regulations to halt the lev fall, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said.
-- Fuel prices in Bulgaria are expected to rise by 24 percent effective from November 30 because of last week's sharp fall in the lev, the newspaper said without qouting sources. @
-- Bulgaria may receive wheat and fodder deliveries from Germany as a humanitarian aid, Bulgaria's president-elect Petar Stoyanov upon return from an official visit to Berlin.
-- The Russian-Bulgarian gas joint venture Topenergy will propose to Bulgaria's Energy Ministry a barter of natural gas against Bulgarian foods, a Topenergy official said.
-- Sofia's mayor Stefan Sofianski agreed the sale of a stake in Sofia's Municipal Bank to the Moscow Municipal Bank with Moscow's mayor, an Bulgarian official said.

-- Foreign companies have invested some $60 million in Bulgaria in the last three months and investments for the whole 1996 are expected to total $300 million, a senior official from Bulgaria's Foreign Investment Agency said.
-- Three private and 14 state companies will vie for export quotas for a total of 30,000 tonnes of cooking oil, Bulgaria's Agriculture ministry said.

-- The cabinet will not seek a default on Bulgaria's foreign debt payments because it stands no chance to win thousands of potential lawsuits that might be filed by investors in Bulgarian Brady bonds, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
